paper.title: Wearable heart-rate monitoring in older adults: accuracy of wrist sensors

paper_text:
Wearable heart-rate monitoring in older adults: accuracy of wrist sensors
Nguyen, T., Cole, R.  Journal of Fake Cardiology, 2020

Abstract
Wrist-worn optical sensors estimated heart rate in 200 adults aged 70 or over to within 4.8 beats per minute of ECG.

alerts.description: A retraction notice was published for this paper.

documents.text:
Retraction: Wearable heart-rate monitoring in older adults: accuracy of wrist sensors

This article has been retracted at the authors' request because it substantially duplicates a paper they published earlier (Nguyen and Cole, 2019, doi 10.9999/fake.2019.130). The data and findings are the same as in the earlier paper, which remains in the literature. The editors found no problem with the data themselves.

draft_text:
Choosing a wearable for a falls-prevention trial

1. Introduction
Wrist-worn sensors can estimate heart rate to within about 5 beats per minute in older adults (Alvarez et al., 2018; Nguyen and Cole, 2020; Farouk, 2021).

References
Alvarez, M. et al. (2018). Optical heart-rate sensing at rest. J Fake Biomed Eng.
Farouk, H. (2021). Sensors for older people. Fake Geriatrics Rev.
Nguyen, T., & Cole, R. (2020). Wearable heart rate monitoring in older adults. J Fake Cardiol, 14(2).

must_include: says the retraction is for duplicate publication, not for errors or misconduct in the data
says the findings still stand in the original publication
advises keeping the citation and citing the retraction notice or the original paper
must_not_include: says the data were fabricated or unreliable
recommends deleting the sentence or the claim it supports

expected.why: Rubric: a retraction for duplicate publication = medium, and the action is to keep the citation and cite the notice/original copy. The draft cites it in a group of three with an abbreviated journal name and a shortened title, so it must still be found (cited true). supporting x medium = low. The trap is 'retraction' = high = remove.
